sections.text_helper: Section 31.6.23 "TIM capture/compare mode register 3 (TIM_CCMR3)" in chapter 31 (Advanced-control timers (TIM1/TIM8)), RM0522 Rev 1, page 1104.
sections.section_content:
Address offset: 0x050
Reset value: 0x0000 0000
Refer to the above CCMR1 register description. Channels 5 and 6 can only be configured in
output.
Bits 31:26 Reserved, must be kept at reset value.
Bits 23:18 Reserved, must be kept at reset value.
Bit 15 OC6CE: Output compare 6 clear enable
0: tim_oc6ref is not affected by the tim_ocref_clr_int signal
1: tim_oc6ref is cleared as soon as a High level is detected on tim_ocref_clr_int signal
(tim_ocref_clr input or tim_etrf input)
Note: This mode is not available for all PWM modes. Refer to Section31.3.23: Clearing the
tim_ocxref signal on an external event for the list of forbidden configurations.
Bits 25:24, 14:12 OC6M[4:0]: Output compare 6 mode
Refer to OC5M[4:0] bit description
Bit 11 OC6PE: Output compare 6 preload enable
0:Preload register on TIM_CCR6 disabled. TIM_CCR6 can be written at anytime, the new
value is taken in account immediately.
1:Preload register on TIM_CCR6 enabled. Read/Write operations access the preload
register. TIM_CCR6 preload value is loaded in the active register at each update event.
These bits can not be modified as long as LOCK level 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in
TIM_BDTR register) and CC1S = 00 (the channel is configured in output).
Bit 10 OC6FE: Output compare 6 fast enable
This bit decreases the latency between a trigger event and a transition on the timer output. It
must be used in one-pulse mode (OPM bit set in TIM_CR1 register), to have the output pulse
starting as soon as possible after the starting trigger.
0:CC6 behaves normally depending on counter and CCR6 values even when the trigger is
ON. The minimum delay to activate CC6 output when an edge occurs on the trigger input
is 5 clock cycles.
1:An active edge on the trigger input acts like a compare match on CC6 output. Then, OC is
set to the compare level independently from the result of the comparison. Delay to sample
the trigger input and to activate CC6 output is reduced to 3 clock cycles. OCFE acts only if
the channel is configured in PWM1 or PWM2 mode.
Bits 9:8 Reserved, must be kept at reset value.
Bit 7 OC5CE: Output compare 5 clear enable
0: tim_oc5ref is not affected by the tim_ocref_clr_int signal
1: tim_oc5ref is cleared as soon as a High level is detected on tim_ocref_clr_int signal
(tim_ocref_clr input or tim_etrf input)
Note: This mode is not available for all PWM modes. Refer to Section31.3.23: Clearing the
tim_ocxref signal on an external event for the list of forbidden configurations.
Bits 17:16, 6:4 OC5M[4:0]: Output compare 5 mode
These bits define the behavior of the output reference signal tim_oc5ref5. tim_oc5ref is
active high whereas tim_oc5 active level depends on CC5P bit.
00000:Frozen - The comparison between the output compare register TIM_CCR5 and the
counter TIM_CNT has no effect on the outputs.(this mode is used to generate a timing
base).
00001:Set channel 5 to active level on match. tim_oc5ref signal is forced high when the
counter TIM_CNT matches the capture/compare register 5 (TIM_CCR5).
00010:Set channel 5 to inactive level on match. tim_oc5ref signal is forced low when the
counter TIM_CNT matches the capture/compare register 5 (TIM_CCR5).
00011:Toggle - tim_oc5ref toggles when TIM_CNT = TIM_CCR5.
00100:Force inactive level - tim_oc5ref is forced low.
00101:Force active level - tim_oc5ref is forced high.
00110:PWM mode 1 - In upcounting, channel 5 is active as long as TIM_CNT<TIM_CCR5
else inactive. In downcounting, channel 5 is inactive (tim_oc5ref = 0) as long as
TIM_CNT>TIM_CCR5 else active (tim_oc5ref = 1).
00111:PWM mode 2 - In upcounting, channel 5 is inactive as long as TIM_CNT<TIM_CCR5
else active. In downcounting, channel 5 is active as long as TIM_CNT>TIM_CCR5
else inactive.
01000:Retrigerrable OPM mode 1 - In up-counting mode, the channel is active until a trigger
event is detected (on tim_trgi signal). Then, a comparison is performed as in PWM
mode 1 and the channels becomes active again at the next update. In down-counting
mode, the channel is inactive until a trigger event is detected (on tim_trgi signal).
Then, a comparison is performed as in PWM mode 1 and the channels becomes
inactive again at the next update.
01001:Retrigerrable OPM mode 2 - In up-counting mode, the channel is inactive until a
trigger event is detected (on tim_trgi signal). Then, a comparison is performed as in
PWM mode 2 and the channels becomes inactive again at the next update. In down-
counting mode, the channel is active until a trigger event is detected (on tim_trgi
signal). Then, a comparison is performed as in PWM mode 1 and the channels
becomes active again at the next update.
01010-01011:Reserved.
01100-01101:Combined PWM mode 1 and 2. Refer to Table296 for details.
01110-01111:Asymmetric PWM mode 1 and 2. Refer to Table295 for details.
Others: Reserved
Note: These bits can not be modified as long as LOCK level 3 has been programmed (LOCK
bits in TIM_BDTR register) and CC1S = 00 (the channel is configured in output).
Note: In PWM mode, the OCREF level changes only when the result of the comparison
changes or when the output compare mode switches from “frozen” mode to “PWM”
mode.
Bit 3 OC5PE: Output compare 5 preload enable
0:Preload register on TIM_CCR5 disabled. TIM_CCR5 can be written at anytime, the new
value is taken in account immediately.
1:Preload register on TIM_CCR5 enabled. Read/Write operations access the preload
register. TIM_CCR5 preload value is loaded in the active register at each update event.
These bits can not be modified as long as LOCK level 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in
TIM_BDTR register) and CC1S = 00 (the channel is configured in output).
Bit 2 OC5FE: Output compare 5 fast enable
This bit decreases the latency between a trigger event and a transition on the timer output. It
must be used in one-pulse mode (OPM bit set in TIM_CR1 register), to have the output pulse
starting as soon as possible after the starting trigger.
0:CC5 behaves normally depending on counter and CCR5 values even when the trigger is
ON. The minimum delay to activate CC5 output when an edge occurs on the trigger input
is 5 clock cycles.
1:An active edge on the trigger input acts like a compare match on CC5 output. Then, OC is
set to the compare level independently from the result of the comparison. Delay to sample
the trigger input and to activate CC5 output is reduced to 3 clock cycles. OCFE acts only if
the channel is configured in PWM1 or PWM2 mode.
Bits 1:0 Reserved, must be kept at reset value.
